intro.text: Sustainable Development Goal 1 (SDG 1), “No Poverty,” aims to end poverty in all its forms everywhere. Poverty reduction requires more than direct financial assistance; it also involves improving access to education, healthcare, employment, skill development, financial services, entrepreneurship opportunities, social protection and community resources.

Kalinga University, Naya Raipur, contributes to the objectives of SDG 1 through a range of academic, community outreach and institutional initiatives. During the academic year 2024–25, the University's activities reflected an integrated approach to poverty reduction through access to education, scholarships, financial literacy, entrepreneurship development, employability enhancement, rural engagement, healthcare support, legal awareness and livelihood-oriented skill development.

Scholarships and Access to Higher Education
One of the strongest institutional mechanisms supporting SDG 1 is the provision and promotion of scholarships.

The Toppers Felicitation Ceremony 2025 was organized to recognize meritorious students and make them aware of Kalinga University's scholarship schemes. The programme specifically provided 100% scholarships to the top 10 CBSE and CGBSE rank holders of Class XII in Chhattisgarh, along with cash prizes and merit certificates. Students securing 80% and above were also made aware of the University's scholarship policy.
The event recorded 135 student participants and 85 parents, making a total participation of 220. The report further states that 27 toppers and other high-performing students participated.

The scholarship initiative helps reduce financial barriers to higher education and provides meritorious students with an opportunity to pursue university education. By reducing the economic burden associated with higher education, such initiatives can contribute to breaking intergenerational cycles of socioeconomic disadvantage.
Financial literacy is an important component of economic resilience and poverty prevention. Kalinga University conducted several programmes related to financial awareness during 2024–25.

The Workshop on Investment Awareness, organized by the Faculty of Commerce and Management on 30 September 2024, focused on financial literacy, investment vehicles, risk assessment and financial planning.

The programme enabled participants to understand different investment options, assess risks, understand market trends and develop financial plans. The report records 78 student participants and 3 faculty participants.
The programme supports financial empowerment by improving participants' ability to make informed financial decisions and plan for their financial future.

blocks.text: Entrepreneurship provides an important pathway towards self-employment, income generation and job creation.
Kalinga University's annual report documents several entrepreneurship-oriented activities.
Entrepreneurship & Innovation as a Career Opportunity

The programme introduced students to entrepreneurship and innovation as career opportunities. The session emphasized business planning, financial management, marketing, leadership, risk management, networking and social responsibility. The report records 81 students and 18 faculty members as participants.

blocks.text: Based strictly on the Annual Reports, the following major outcomes can be highlighted:
Scholarship initiatives, particularly the provision of 100% scholarships to top rank holders, support access to higher education and reduce financial barriers for meritorious students.
Investment awareness and finance-related programmes improved students' understanding of investment options, risk assessment, financial planning, taxation and financial-sector employment.

Entrepreneurship programmes equipped students with business planning, financial management, marketing, innovation and risk-management skills. Ideathon 4.0 additionally created connections with investors and incubation opportunities.
Programmes such as Job Ready for BFSI and GST workshops developed industry-oriented knowledge and job-readiness competencies.
The UBA Gram Sabha directly addressed rural employment, labour rights, minimum wages, skill development and government schemes such as MGNREGA and PMKVY.
The Nukkad Natak and door-to-door campaign increased community awareness regarding rights, legal aid and women's empowerment and collected information on local needs.
Free health camps provided screening, diagnosis, counselling and preventive healthcare. The September 2024 camp alone recorded 282 beneficiaries, while the November camp assessed 124 persons.
The Candle Making Workshop provided practical production skills along with pricing, branding and marketing knowledge, giving participants exposure to a potential micro-enterprise pathway.
